'''Devin Green''' (born October 25, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Hampton Pirates men's basketball|Hampton Pirates]], finishing in 2005. After his tenure at Hampton University, he joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–2006 season]].

==Professional career==
He was [[undrafted]] out of [[Hampton University]], and was signed by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] as a free agent, appearing in 27 games in the 2005–2006 season. On October 30, 2006, he was waived by the Lakers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/transactions/oct2006_trans.html NBA.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>  Green played for the [[NBDL]] team the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] halfway through the season of 2006–07, but then left for the [[Basketball Bundesliga|German Basketball League]] team [[RheinEnergie Köln]]. As a member of RheinEnergie Köln, he won the 2006–07 German National Cup and helped reach the German national championship semi-finals.

He signed a contract with the [[Miami Heat]] on August 11, 2007, but was waived on October 29, 2007, from the team. In February 2008, he signed for the [[Serie A (basketball)|Italian First Division]] team of [[Siviglia Wear Teramo]].

Green made another attempt to enter the NBA with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in 2008 but was cut a week before the start of the regular season.<ref>[http://www.sportingnews.com/nba/articles/20081023/1065290-p.html Associated Press/SportingNews.com: Spurs waive 3 to put roster at 16, October 23, 2008]{{Dead link|date=January 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2008-09 San Antonio Spurs Transactions |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/SAS/2009_transactions.html |access-date=2026-02-21 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He signed with [[Base Oostende]], a top Belgian League club on October 31, 2008.

Green reported to Las Vegas on July 9, 2009, to participate in the 2009 NBA Summer League as a member of the [http://www.nba.com/summerleague2009/team/index.jsp?team=timberwolves Minnesota Timberwolves.]  Green's summer was the subject of a documentary titled "Devin Green: The Journey."  The first four episodes are currently available on YouTube and at [http://www.DevinGreen.tumblr.com Green's Website].

In January 2011 he signed with [[PBC Lukoil Academic]] in Bulgaria.<ref>[http://www.lukoilacademic.net/page.php?n=137824&SiteID=450 ЛУКОЙЛ Академик се подсили с още две нови попълнения] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721124247/http://www.lukoilacademic.net/page.php?n=137824&SiteID=450 |date=2011-07-21 }} {{in lang|bg}}</ref>

During the 2011–12 season, Green played with the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] and [[Idaho Stampede]] of the NBA D-League.

In the summer of 2012, Green re-signed with [[PBC Lukoil Academic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/other-leagues/40762/lukoil-academic-sofia-announced-devin-green.html |title=Lukoil Academic Sofia announced Devin Green |publisher=Sportando.net |date=2012-07-09 |accessdate=2013-04-03}}</ref> In January 2013, he was released.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/other-leagues/49980/lukoil-academic-released-devin-green.html |title=Lukoil Academic released Devin Green |publisher=Sportando.net |date=2013-01-25 |accessdate=2013-04-03}}</ref> Later that month he signed with [[Spirou Charleroi]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/belgium/50317/spirou-charleroi-signs-devin-green.html |title=Spirou Charleroi signs Devin Green |publisher=Sportando.net |date=2013-01-31 |accessdate=2013-04-03}}</ref> He parted ways with Spirou Charleroi in March 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Spirou Charleroi, Devin Green part ways|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/belgium/115061/spirou-charleroi-devin-green-part-ways.html|accessdate=27 March 2014|newspaper=Sportando.com}}</ref> He then signed with [[Guaros de Lara (basketball)|Guaros de Lara]] of Venezuela.<ref>{{cite news|title=Guaros de Lara replace Smush Parker with Devin Green|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/115236/guaros-de-lara-replace-smush-parker-with-devin-green.html|accessdate=27 March 2014|newspaper=Sportando.com}}</ref> In April 2015, he left Guaros de Lara.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/159473/dewarick-spencer-moves-to-guaros-de-lara.html Dewarick Spencer moves to Guaros de Lara]</ref>

In June, 2019, Green comeback to the [[Wuhan Dangdai]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Devin Green is back at Wuhan |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Qatar/news/580667/Devin-Green-is-back-at-Wuhan |publisher=Eurobasket.com |access-date=25 September 2024 |date=5 June 2019}}</ref>

In the end of 2019, Green played for [[MC Alger (basketball)|GS Pétroliers]] in the [[Road to BAL]] and helped the team win the West Division and qualify for the [[2021 BAL season]].
